battery_overview: The Forensic Language Analysis Battery analyzes a question–answer turn-pair from a legal deposition for structural properties, force dynamics, and strategic distortion. It examines how agency and power are distributed, how pressure and leverage operate, what evidential ground the claims rest on, how stable that ground is, and what strategic exposure exists. Five sequential LLM calls produce the analysis. Call 6 distills everything into a two-word pattern declaration — identical in structure to all other CA_15 batteries.

pattern_field.label: Pattern Declaration
pattern_field.definition: A two-word label capturing the dominant forensic dynamic of the exchange. Derived after all five analytical calls are computed and represents the instrument's single synthesized judgment about what structural and strategic event occurred. Not a summary of content — a label for the kind of force or distortion that defined the exchange.
pattern_field.why_it_matters: When read in sequence across hundreds of turn-pairs, these pattern declarations reveal the higher-order structure of how force, pressure, and distortion moved through the entire deposition.
pattern_field.examples: Deflection Contest, Frame Capture, Blame Shift, Authority Press

fields.label: Agency Distribution
fields.definition: How agency — the capacity to act, decide, and influence — is allocated across the three possible sites in the exchange. Turn 1 and Turn 2 receive integer percentages (0–100); External receives the remainder and is labeled when non-zero. The flow keys identify which site agency moves from and which it moves toward.
fields.scale: Structured object: turn_1 (0–100) · turn_2 (0–100) · external (0–100, sums to 100) · external_label (text or null) · flow_from ('speaker_1' | 'speaker_2' | 'external') · flow_to ('speaker_1' | 'speaker_2' | 'external')
fields.why_it_matters: Identifies where decision-making power and responsibility are located in the exchange, and in which direction they are moving.

fields.label: Power Alignment
fields.definition: The power posture each speaker adopts and what that posture is directed toward. For each turn, 3–5 adjective–target pairs are identified. The adjective describes the quality of the power stance; the target names what or who it is aimed at — participants, institutions, groups, or entities discussed in the exchange.
fields.scale: Structured object: turn_1_power_posture [{adjective, target} × 3–5] · turn_2_power_posture [{adjective, target} × 3–5]
fields.why_it_matters: Maps the relational dynamics of power within the exchange — who is asserting, deferring, challenging, or positioning against whom.

fields.label: Blame Structure
fields.definition: Whether blame is present in the exchange and how it is structured. Blame state classifies the form of blame. When blame is present, target names the recipient, justification_type identifies the logic used to support the blame, and intensity scores its strength on the 1–10 scale. All three conditional fields are null when blame_state is 'absent'.
fields.why_it_matters: Tracks how culpability is attributed or avoided, revealing strategic positioning around liability and responsibility.

fields.label: Pressure Configuration
fields.definition: Whether pressure is applied in the exchange, what kind it is, who applies it, who receives it, and how strong it is. When pressure_present is false, all four conditional fields (pressure_type, source, target, intensity) are null. Intensity is scored on the 1–10 scale.
fields.scale: pressure_present: boolean · pressure_type: 'temporal' | 'social' | 'epistemic' | 'material' | 'reputational' · source (text) · target (text) · intensity: 1–10 or null
fields.why_it_matters: Identifies the coercive forces operating in the exchange — what kind of pressure is being applied, by whom, against whom, and at what force.

fields.label: Leverage Pattern
fields.definition: Whether leverage is used in the exchange, what kind, who wields it, who it is applied to, and how strong it is. When leverage_present is false, all four conditional fields are null. Intensity is scored on the 1–10 scale.
fields.scale: leverage_present: boolean · leverage_type: 'authority' | 'information' | 'relationship' | 'resource' | 'expertise' · wielded_by (text) · applied_to (text) · intensity: 1–10 or null
fields.why_it_matters: Reveals what structural advantages are being deployed to shape the exchange's outcome and who holds the upper hand.

fields.label: Accountability State
fields.definition: How accountability is distributed across the exchange. The distribution_pattern classifies the structural form. Holders is an array of entity names when accountability is locatable; null when obscured. Displaced_to names the displacement target when the pattern is 'displaced'; null otherwise.
fields.scale: distribution_pattern: 'concentrated' | 'distributed' | 'displaced' | 'obscured' | 'contested' · holders: [text] or null · displaced_to: text or null
fields.why_it_matters: Shows whether responsibility is being owned, shared, evaded, or redirected — a key forensic indicator of strategic intent.

fields.label: Evidential Basis
fields.definition: What kind of evidence supports the claims made in the exchange, how strong that evidence is, and whether the source is made explicit. When source_explicit is false, gap_description captures the nature of the evidentiary gap in 2–4 words. Gap_description is null when the source is explicit.
fields.scale: basis_type: 'empirical' | 'testimonial' | 'logical' | 'authoritative' | 'assumed' | 'none' · strength: 'strong' | 'moderate' | 'weak' | 'absent' · source_explicit: boolean · gap_description: text (2–4 words) or null
fields.why_it_matters: Assesses the factual foundation of claims — whether they are grounded, inferred, assumed, or unattributed.

fields.label: Source Position
fields.definition: The structural position of the claim's source — who is speaking and from what epistemic vantage point. Credibility markers are 0–3 short phrases identifying features that establish or undermine authority. Distance from event captures how many removes the source is from the events being described.
fields.why_it_matters: Positions the speaker epistemically — how close are they to the truth they are asserting, and what gives them the right to assert it.

fields.label: Inferential Structure
fields.definition: Whether inference is used to bridge claims to conclusions. When inference_present is false, all four conditional fields (inference_type, steps_explicit, missing_steps, strength) are null. When present, steps_explicit identifies whether the reasoning chain is stated or only implied, and missing_steps names the gap in 2–4 words.
fields.scale: inference_present: boolean · inference_type: 'deductive' | 'inductive' | 'abductive' | 'analogical' | 'speculative' · steps_explicit: boolean · missing_steps: text (2–4 words) or null · strength: 'strong' | 'moderate' | 'weak'
fields.why_it_matters: Identifies logical leaps and reasoning gaps — where the argument is solid, where it is implied, and where it can be attacked.

fields.label: Epistemic Reliability
fields.definition: The internal structural durability of the claim — independent of external challenge. Reliability_state classifies the overall condition. Support_structure lists 1–3 short phrases identifying what holds the claim up. Vulnerability_points lists 0–3 phrases identifying where the claim could internally collapse.
fields.why_it_matters: Measures how structurally sound a claim is from the inside — its internal consistency, not just how others are attacking it.

fields.label: Contestability
fields.definition: Whether the claim is being externally attacked or challenged within the exchange. When contest_present is false, all three conditional fields (contest_type, contested_by, contest_strength) are null. Contest_strength scores the challenge's force on the 1–10 scale.
fields.scale: contest_present: boolean · contest_type: 'factual' | 'interpretive' | 'normative' | 'procedural' · contested_by: text or null · contest_strength: 1–10 or null
fields.why_it_matters: Identifies where and how the truth is being actively attacked — who is challenging what, and how hard.

fields.label: Distortion Pattern
fields.definition: Whether the truth is being bent, suppressed, amplified, or substituted in the exchange. When distortion_present is false, all four conditional fields are null. Direction classifies whether the distortion benefits the speaker ('favorable'), harms them ('unfavorable'), or is directionally neutral. Intensity scored 1–10.
fields.scale: distortion_present: boolean · distortion_type: 'amplification' | 'minimization' | 'reframing' | 'omission' | 'substitution' · what_is_distorted: text or null · direction: 'favorable' | 'unfavorable' | 'neutral_shift' · intensity: 1–10 or null
fields.why_it_matters: Detects strategic manipulation of truth — whether facts are being exaggerated, minimized, replaced, or recontextualized to serve a positional interest.

fields.label: Concealment State
fields.definition: Whether information is being strategically withheld or obscured. When concealment_present is false, all three conditional fields (concealment_mechanism, what_is_concealed, intensity) are null. What_is_concealed names the suppressed content in 2–4 words. Intensity scored 1–10.
fields.scale: concealment_present: boolean · concealment_mechanism: 'omission' | 'vagueness' | 'misdirection' | 'technical_obscurity' | 'temporal_displacement' · what_is_concealed: text (2–4 words) or null · intensity: 1–10 or null
fields.why_it_matters: Identifies what is being hidden and how — the gap between what was said and what was strategically withheld.

fields.label: Framing Bias
fields.definition: Whether the exchange is structured around a directionally biased frame. When bias_present is false, all three conditional fields (bias_direction, framing_elements, intensity) are null. Framing_elements lists 2–4 short phrases identifying the constitutive components of the bias. Intensity scored 1–10.
fields.scale: bias_present: boolean · bias_direction: 'self_advantaging' | 'blame_shifting' | 'protective_framing' | 'accusatory_framing' · framing_elements: [text × 2–4] or null · intensity: 1–10 or null
fields.why_it_matters: Reveals the directional slant of the exchange — whether it is constructed to protect, accuse, deflect, or advantage.

fields.label: Adversarial Posture
fields.definition: The adversarial stance taken in the exchange. Posture_type classifies the overall orientation. Tactical_moves is an array of 0–3 specific maneuvers used within that posture. Target_of_posture names what the posture is directed at in 2–4 words; null when posture_type is 'cooperative' or 'neutral'.
fields.scale: posture_type: 'cooperative' | 'neutral' | 'defensive' | 'aggressive' | 'evasive' · tactical_moves: ['preemption' | 'deflection' | 'counter_accusation' | 'boundary_setting' | 'challenge' | 'none'] × 0–3 · target_of_posture: text (2–4 words) or null
fields.why_it_matters: Classifies the overall adversarial stance and specific tactical maneuvers — whether the speaker is attacking, defending, evading, or cooperating, and exactly how.
